node.statement: Let U=I-T and X=T-I=-U. Since ||T||<1/3, the Neumann series sum_{k>=0} T^k converges absolutely and is U^(-1). Also W:=X^2-I=U^2-I=-2T+T^2 has ||W||<=2||T||+||T||^2<7/9<1, so the registered binomial power series defining (X^2)^(-1/2) converges absolutely. In the scalar disc |z|<1/3, the branch normalized to 1 at z=0 satisfies ((1-z)^2)^(-1/2)=(1-z)^(-1)=sum_{k>=0}z^k: indeed Re(1-z)>0, so the normalized square root of (1-z)^2 is 1-z. Thus the two sides have identical Taylor series at 0; evaluating these absolutely convergent series at the single Banach-algebra element T gives (X^2)^(-1/2)=U^(-1).
